summary: Independently verified the Telegram login widget blink fix on /safedeal/signin. Marked the initial Telegram <iframe> with a data attribute, installed a MutationObserver on the host element [aria-label="Log in with Telegram"], then typed a 21-character email character-by-character to force many parent re-renders (each keystroke changes parent state and passes a new inline onSuccess closure). After ~4s of observation post-typing: original iframe node still attached (document.contains === true), initial-marker still present, iframeCountInHost === 1, and the MutationObserver recorded 0 childList mutations (0 iframe removals, 0 iframe re-adds). This confirms the widget is injected exactly once and is NOT re-created on parent re-renders — the blinking bug is resolved. 'Bot domain invalid' message appears as expected (preview host not registered with Telegram bot) and does not affect the fix.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix in Components/SafeDeal/TelegramLoginButton.tsx is correct: injection effect depends only on [bot] and callbacks are read from handlersRef, preventing re-injection on parent re-render. Keeping the host Box mounted and only toggling CSS display during busy state is the right pattern.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Telegram widget blink fix on SafeDeal signin is verified. Measured: 0 iframe removals/adds during 21 keystrokes + 4s observation, original iframe node preserved. Same shared component is also used in Components/SafeDeal/Home/TelegramAlertsCard.tsx (mode='link') behind auth — not retested but uses identical fixed component.
rca of the issue: Previous bug: injection useEffect in TelegramLoginButton.tsx depended on inline callback props whose identity changed on every parent render, causing host.innerHTML wipe and iframe re-creation on every keystroke -> visible blink. Fix: effect deps reduced to [bot]; callbacks accessed via a mutable ref (handlersRef). Verified in this run.
